stories.headline: Bezos spent $75 million on Melania film rights and marketing
stories.summary: Jeff Bezos paid $40 million for the rights to the Melania film and is spending another $35 million to market it, a small fraction of his net worth.
stories.text: Last night, Donald Trump attended the premiere of Melania at the newly renamed Trump Kennedy Center, a film following Melania Trump ahead of Trump's second inauguration. Amazon founder In part-time Maui resident Jeff Bezos paid $40 million for the film rights and is shelling out another $35 million to market a vanity project that no one really cares about. That's a lot of money, but for Bezos, it represents a mere pittance, less than three-tenths of 1% of the net worth of Bezos, which is more than $280 billion, according to Forbes.

stories.headline: Wealthy travelers increasingly drive Hawaiʻi tourism, pricing out middle class
stories.summary: A new study says the top 10% of U.S. households account for over half of leisure travel spending, and Hawaiʻi tourism increasingly caters to them while middle-income visitors feel priced out.
stories.text: Three out of four of the world's wealthiest men and one of America's wealthiest women live or have property on our neighbor islands. More and more, Maui is becoming a playground for the rich. A new study shows the top 10% of U.S. households now account for over half of all leisure travel spending, $544 billion, according to Bead of Hawaiʻi. Hawaiʻi's Tourism is increasingly built to cater to these high-spending, frequent travelers rather than middle-class families. As airfare, hotel, rental car, and hidden fee costs keep rising, many middle-income visitors feel priced out. Hawaiʻi travel no longer feels attainable, the way it once did, they say.

stories.headline: Police shoot and kill armed man in Wailuku field
stories.summary: Maui police shot and killed a man with a firearm in an open field in Wailuku after he reportedly did not respond to an officer's command and opened fire, and the officers are on administrative leave.
stories.text: At around 7.30 last night, a report came in to Maui police that a man with a firearm was spotted in an open field in Wailuku, ʻOf Kuikahi Drive. Reportedly, the man did not respond to an officer's command and opened fire. The officers returned fire and shot the man, who died at the scene. His name was not released pending notification of next of kin. The investigation remains ongoing, with details still preliminary. Officers involved have been placed on administrative leave per standard procedure.

stories.headline: Former Maui traffic cop Taguma has bench warrant on Kauaʻi
stories.summary: Court records show Taguma, the former Maui traffic officer, got a driving citation on Kauaʻi last July, skipped court, and has a bench warrant out for him.
stories.text: Remember Taguma? He was an infamous Maui policeman who was demoted to traffic cop because he accidentally shot himself in the foot. He had a reputation for coming out of nowhere in his go-kart to give you a ticket. He handed out an enormous amount of violations and reportedly even ticketed his own mother. His antics even sparked citizens to launch the online platform called Taguma Watch, now Maui Watch, to monitor his whereabouts. Well, court records show that in July of last year, Taguma got an inattention to driving citation on Kauaʻi. He never showed up in court and there was a bench warrant out for him.

stories.text: ʻAkakū will kick off its 2026 Akakū Upstairs Salon Series next Thursday, January 15th at 6 p.m. with a fun critique of the top films of 2025.
